statement: Real-world chaotic systems exhibit class-dependent spectral behavior, where structured systems produce significant alpha deviation from null models, while noise-dominated systems do not.
why_it_matters: If true, this suggests the presence of a universal structural signature in real-world chaos.
how_to_break: Run the pipeline on independent datasets and observe alpha collapse to noise
Demonstrate alpha instability across seeds or runtime environments
Show that null models produce equivalent or stronger alpha signals

minimal_test.input: Any real-world chaotic time series dataset
minimal_test.process: Run spectral estimation using the provided pipeline
minimal_test.expected: alpha remains stable within defined tolerance
minimal_test.falsification: alpha varies randomly or aligns with null distributions
